tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. /-- Decidability of `TransferExcl` (WC4 C22.3). -/
instance (L : MutexLayout) (st : SC × SyncReg) (src : Nat) : Decidable (TransferExcl L st src) := by
  unfold TransferExcl; infer_instance

/-- WC4 C22.3 for the transfers of the by-value composite (WC4 C23):
the source of every transfer phase satisfies `TransferExcl` in the state where that phase starts
(WC4 C5.2), the registry being `reg`. -/
def EncapVals (L : MutexLayout) (reg : SyncReg) (c : Nat) : SC → List (Nat × Nat) → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | t, v :: vs => TransferExcl L (t, reg) v.1 ∧ EncapVals L reg c (transferEffC t c v.1 v.2) vs

/-- Encapsulation of one step in state `st` (hypothesis on traces, WC4 C22, C23): for each live
entry, WC4 C22.1 (`derive`, `split`), C22.2 (raw `deriveSync`), C22.3 (`transfer`, and the
transfer phases of the by-value composite) and C22.5 (`endUse` whose place is the controller leaf
`ctl` or a strict structural subplace of `slot`). WC4 C22.4 (controller-write protocol) is a
realization/interface obligation (WC4 C22) with no content in `S_C`, which has no values (Spec 1
§41), and is not represented. -/
def Encap (L : MutexLayout) (st : SC × SyncReg) : Label → Prop
  | .kernel _ (.derive src _ _) => ∀ e ∈ st.2, e.Live st.1 → src ≠ e.guarded
  | .kernel _ (.split src _) => ∀ e ∈ st.2, e.Live st.1 → src ≠ e.guarded
  | .kernel _ (.transfer src _) => TransferExcl L st src
  | .kernel _ (.endUse p) => ∀ e ∈ st.2, e.Live st.1 → ControlOf L st.1 e ≠ some p ∧
      OptP (slotOf st.1 e.guarded) (fun q => partOf st.1.P p q → p = q) True
  | .spawnVal c _ ls vs => EncapVals L st.2 c (spawnCreate st.1 c ls) vs
  | .deriveSync _ g => ∀ e ∈ st.2, e.Live st.1 → g ≠ e.guarded
  | _ => True

/-- Runs of labelled steps. -/
inductive LRun (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) :
    SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → List Label → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → Prop where
  | nil {st : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} : LRun k L st [] st
  | cons {st st₁ st₂ : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} {lbl : Label} {lbls : List Label} :
      LStep k L lbl st st₁ → LRun k L st₁ lbls st₂ → LRun k L st (lbl :: lbls) st₂

/-- `EncapsulatedTrace` (WC4 C22, C23: "Any lemma conditional on encapsulation must expose that
condition in its theorem statement or the reachable-trace assumptions"): a run every step of which
satisfies `Encap` in the state where it is taken, read on the kernel state and the
synchronization registry. -/
inductive EncapsulatedTrace (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) :
    SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → List Label → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → Prop where
  | nil {st : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} : EncapsulatedTrace k L st [] st
  | cons {st st₁ st₂ : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} {lbl : Label} {lbls : List Label} :
      Encap L (st.1, st.2.1) lbl → LStep k L lbl st st₁ → EncapsulatedTrace k L st₁ lbls st₂ →
      EncapsulatedTrace k L st (lbl :: lbls) st₂

/-- An encapsulated trace is a run. -/
theorem EncapsulatedTrace.run {k : K} {L : MutexLayout} {st st' : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg}
    {lbls : List Label} (h : EncapsulatedTrace k L st lbls st') : LRun k L st lbls st' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact .nil
  | cons _ hs _ ih => exact .cons hs ih

/-- Theorem 1 (WC4 C14, C24): in a state whose registry has no live entry, the obligation of WC4
C14 makes `K_C.SyncAuthorized` false on that registry. Fragment: every state, single-context ones
included. -/
theorem syncAuthorized_false {kc : KC SyncReg} {reg : SyncReg} {s : SC}
    (hsound : SyncSound kc reg s) (hnone : ∀ e ∈ reg, ¬ e.Live s) (g f : Nat) :
    ¬ kc.SyncAuthorized reg s g f := fun h => by

def NewMutexOk (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (ar : ArenaReg) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c g : Nat)
    (st' : SC × SyncReg) : Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ NewMutexPre k L ar s reg c g ∧ st' = (s, reg ++ [⟨g, none⟩])

/-- `acquire` on entry `i` executed by `c` (WC4 C16): with the library instantiation of
`SyncAuthorized` for the entry, `deriveSync(guarded)` on the registry `reg` and the record of the
fresh grant identity `|A|` in the entry. A taken controller (`grant ≠ none`) leaves `acquire` not
enabled; WC4 C16 states no other outcome than success, so only `ok` is defined. -/
def AcquireOk (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c i : Nat)
    (st' : SC × SyncReg) : Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ ∃ e, reg[i]? = some e ∧ EntryAuth L s e (s.view c).top ∧
    DeriveSyncPre (libKC k L) reg s c e.guarded ∧
    st' = (deriveSyncEff s c e.guarded, reg.set i { e with grant := some s.A.length })

/-- `unlock` of entry `i` executed by `c` (WC4 C17.1–C17.4): O3 releases the grant and the registry
records `grant = none` (WC4 C17 effect). C17.2 and C17.3 are the preconditions of O3 (Spec 1 §62);
C17.4 is `CtrlRight`. The controller update is a realization obligation (WC4 C17), not a
precondition; only `ok` is defined. -/
def UnlockOk (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c i : Nat) (st' : SC × SyncReg) :
    Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ ∃ e g, reg[i]? = some e ∧ e.Live s ∧ e.grant = some g ∧ ReleasePre (s.view c) g ∧
    CtrlRight L s e (s.view c).top ∧
    st' = (s.set (releaseEff (s.view c) g), reg.set i { e with grant := none })

/-- `resetLock` of entry `i` executed by `c` (WC4 C18.1–C18.3): the entry becomes available; the
kernel state is unchanged (WC4 C18 effect). WC4 C18.3: "`ControlOf(entry)` resolves to an
existing, usable controller **leaf**, as required by C21.3"; the controller-initialization
invariant is not a precondition (WC4 C18.3: "established separately for every live entry by
C21.7"). Only `ok` is defined. -/
def ResetLockOk (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c i : Nat) (st' : SC × SyncReg) :
    Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ ∃ e, reg[i]? = some e ∧ (s.view c).ExercisableAt e.guarded .modify ∧
    NoCoveringDesc s e.guarded ∧
    OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl => s.flat.Usable ctl ∧ isLeaf s.P ctl) False ∧
    st' = (s, reg.set i { e with grant := none })

/-- No active descendant of `guarded` covers a protected leaf (WC4 C13.9, C18.2, C22). -/
def NoCoveringDesc (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Prop := ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ CoveringDesc s g j

/-- Decidability of `NoCoveringDesc` (WC4 C22). -/
instance (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Decidable (NoCoveringDesc s g) := by
  unfold NoCoveringDesc; infer_instance

/-- `GrantDiscipline` (WC4 C22). -/
def GrantDiscipline (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → e.grant = none → NoCoveringDesc s e.guarded

/-- WC4 C21.4, first clause: distinct live entries (by position in the registry) have distinct
`ControlOf` leaves. -/
def CtlUnique (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i j : Nat) (e e' : SyncEntry) (ctl : Nat), reg[i]? = some e → reg[j]? = some e' →
    e.Live s → e'.Live s → ControlOf L s e = some ctl → ControlOf L s e' = some ctl → i = j

/-- WC4 C21.7, initialization invariant for `slot`: for every live entry, every structural leaf of
the place holding `guarded` is `Init`. -/
def SlotInit (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s →
    OptP (slotOf s e.guarded) (fun q => ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.I l = .init) False

/-- WC4 C21.7, initialization invariant for `ctl`: for every live entry, the controller leaf
`ControlOf(entry)` is `Init`. -/
def CtlInit (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl => s.I ctl = .init) False

/-- `SyncInv` (WC4 C21.1–C21.7): items 1–5 and 7 over live entries, item 6 over every entry. -/
structure SyncInv (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop where
  /-- WC4 C21.1: `guarded` is active (liveness), has own mode `Modify`, and is held by a usable
  place. -/
  guarded : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (s.A[e.guarded]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify ∧
    PlaceUsable s.flat y.holder) False
  /-- WC4 C21.2: a recorded grant exists, has origin `guarded` and footprint
  `footprint(guarded)`. -/

`deriveSync` is a new candidate concurrent transition creating an ordinary derived `Modify` authority from `guarded` over `footprint(guarded)`.

/-- Label of a step of the kernel with the synchronization and arena libraries (WC4 C2, C19,
C23; Spec 1 §76–§78). -/
inductive Label where
  | kernel (c : Nat) (op : KernelOp)
  | spawn (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
  | terminate (c : Nat)
  | join (c d : Nat)
  | deriveSync (c g : Nat)
  | newMutex (c g : Nat)
  | acquire (c i : Nat)
  | unlock (c i : Nat)
  | resetLock (c i : Nat)
  | spawnVal (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) (vs : List (Nat × Nat))
  | newArena (c storage internal : Nat)
  | issue (c arena : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat)
  | reset (c arena : Nat)

/-- Labelled `ok` step of the concurrent kernel with the synchronization and arena libraries
(WC4 C2, C4, C5, C6–C8, C13, C15–C18, C19; WC4 C23 for the by-value composite; Spec 1 §76–§78 for
the arenas): kernel and frame steps keep both registries; raw `deriveSync` runs under the library
instantiation of `SyncAuthorized` on the current registry (WC4 C14); the mutex operations change
the synchronization registry, the arena operations the arena registry (Spec 1 §46). -/
inductive LStep (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) :
    Label → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → Prop where
  | kernel {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} {op : KernelOp} :
      opStepC k op c s (.ok s') → LStep k L (.kernel c op) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | spawn {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} {ps : List Nat}
      {ls : LocalShape} :
      SpawnStep s c ps ls (.ok s') → LStep k L (.spawn c ps ls) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | terminate {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} :
      TermStep k s c (.ok s') → LStep k L (.terminate c) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | join {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c d : Nat} :
      JoinStep s c d (.ok s') → LStep k L (.join c d) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | deriveSync {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c g : Nat} :
      DeriveSyncStep (libKC k L) reg s c g (.ok s') →
      LStep k L (.deriveSync c g) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | newMutex {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c g : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      NewMutexOk k L ar s reg c g st' → LStep k L (.newMutex c g) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | acquire {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      AcquireOk k L s reg c i st' → LStep k L (.acquire c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | unlock {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      UnlockOk L s reg c i st' → LStep k L (.unlock c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | resetLock {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × SyncReg} :
      ResetLockOk L s reg c i st' → LStep k L (.resetLock c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, st'.2, ar)
  | spawnVal {s s' : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c : Nat} {ps : List Nat}
      {ls : LocalShape} {vs : List (Nat × Nat)} :
      SpawnValStep k s c ps ls vs (.ok s') →
      LStep k L (.spawnVal c ps ls vs) (s, reg, ar) (s', reg, ar)
  | newArena {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c st i : Nat} {st' : SC × ArenaReg} :
      NewArenaStepC s reg ar c st i (.ok st') →
      LStep k L (.newArena c st i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, reg, st'.2)
  | issue {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {region : List Nat} {dst : Nat}
      {st' : SC × ArenaReg} :
      IssueStepC k s ar c i region dst (.ok st') →
      LStep k L (.issue c i region dst) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, reg, st'.2)
  | reset {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {ar : ArenaReg} {c i : Nat} {st' : SC × ArenaReg} :
      ResetStepC s ar c i (.ok st') → LStep k L (.reset c i) (s, reg, ar) (st'.1, reg, st'.2)

/-- WC4 C22.3 for the source `src` of a transfer in state `st`: for each live entry, `src` is
neither the place `slot` holding `guarded`, nor a strict structural subplace of `slot`, nor the
controller leaf `ctl`. -/
def TransferExcl (L : MutexLayout) (st : SC × SyncReg) (src : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ st.2, e.Live st.1 →
    OptP (slotOf st.1 e.guarded) (fun q => ¬ partOf st.1.P src q) True ∧
      ControlOf L st.1 e ≠ some src

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §2 W-C22.2, `ok noyau / hors C22.2`: from `MX₄`, context 1 outside
`acquire` takes the raw `deriveSync(guarded)` step under the library instantiation (the facts
C14.1–C14.3 hold); `Encap` excludes it (WC4 C22.2). After the step the registry still records
`grant = none` while an active descendant covers `T`: `GrantDiscipline` fails, and `acquire(e)` is
enabled for neither context in that state (WC4 C13.9, C14: blocking descendant). The corpus adds
"`acquire(e)` plus jamais habilitée"; `W_C22_2_reenable` refutes it. Positive twin: `S2_1_ok`. -/
theorem W_C22_2_encap : DeriveSyncStep (libKC KM L0) regX x4 1 3 (.ok x5) ∧
    ¬ Encap L0 (x4, regX) (.deriveSync 1 3) ∧ ¬ GrantDiscipline x5 regX ∧
    ∀ st', ¬ AcquireOk KM L0 x5 regX 0 0 st' ∧ ¬ AcquireOk KM L0 x5 regX 1 0 st' := by
  refine ⟨⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, fun h => h ⟨3, none⟩ (by decide) (by decide) rfl,
    fun h => (by decide : ¬ NoCoveringDesc x5 3) (h ⟨3, none⟩ (by decide) (by decide) rfl),
    fun st' => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · rintro ⟨-, e, he, -, hpre, -⟩
    cases he; exact (by decide : ¬ DeriveSyncPre (libKC KM L0) regX x5 0 3) hpre
  · rintro ⟨-, e, he, -, hpre, -⟩
    cases he; exact (by decide : ¬ DeriveSyncPre (libKC KM L0) regX x5 1 3) hpre

/-- `c1 : release(g)` of the raw grant of W-C22.2 (O3). -/
def x5r : SC := x5.set (releaseEff (x5.view 1) 5)

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §2 W-C22.2, disagreement with "`acquire(e)` plus jamais habilitée": after
the raw `deriveSync` of `W_C22_2_encap`, context 1 releases the derivative by an ordinary `release`
(O3), an `ok` step that `Encap` admits (WC4 C15 effect: the derivative "is ordinary after
creation … for its … legal release"); `GrantDiscipline` holds again and `acquire(e)` by context 1
is enabled. -/
theorem W_C22_2_reenable : opStepC KM (.release 5) 1 x5 (.ok x5r) ∧
    Encap L0 (x5, regX) (.kernel 1 (.release 5)) ∧ GrantDiscipline x5r regX ∧
    AcquireOk KM L0 x5r regX 1 0 (deriveSyncEff x5r 1 3, [⟨3, some 6⟩]) :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩, trivial,
    fun e he _ _ => by rw [List.mem_singleton.1 he]; decide,
    ⟨by decide, ⟨3, none⟩, rfl, by decide, by decide, rfl⟩⟩

import Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.MX

/-!
# Corpus of milestone 3, case S10

`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10: from `MX₃`, context 0 acquires the grant `g` (held by frame 0), enters
`f1` yielding `m := derive(root_M, Modify)` with a local `M′` of the shape of `M`, and in `f1`
transfers `M` into `M′`. The corpus expects `reject` (O4.7). In the model the step is `ok`
(`S10_1_ok`): the re-indexed §63.7 (`TransferPreC.anchorOrderHeld`) reads `AnchorOrderHeld` on the
moved authorities held by places, and `g` is held by frame 0. The theorem records the state the
corpus describes (the effective anchor of `g` is now in `f1`, which is not an ancestor of frame 0)
and that the exit of `f1` is then rejected. This disagreement is a result, reported, not resolved.
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency.Corpus

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.Concurrency
open Ern.Concurrency.Traces (L0)

/-- `c0 : acquire(e)` in `MX₃`: `g`, authority 4, held by frame 0 (WC4 C16). -/
def r1 : SC := deriveSyncEff x2 0 3
/-- `m := derive(root_M, Modify, footprint(M))`, authority 5 (O1). -/
def r2 : SC := r1.set (deriveEff (r1.view 0) 0 [1, 2] .modify)
/-- `enterFrame f1` yielding `m`, with the local `M′` (place 7, fields 8 and 9, `Uninit`) (O6). -/
def r3 : SC := enterEffC r2 0 [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]
/-- `f1 : transfer(M, M′)` (O4). -/
def r4 : SC := transferEffC r3 0 0 7

/-- The setup of S10 (`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10): `acquire(e)` by context 0, `derive`, then
`enterFrame f1` yielding `m` with the local `M′`. -/
theorem s10_setup : AcquireOk KM L0 x2 regX 0 0 (r1, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) ∧
    opStepC KM (.derive 0 [1, 2] .modify) 0 r1 (.ok r2) ∧
    opStepC KM (.enter [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]) 0 r2 (.ok r3) :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, ⟨3, none⟩, rfl, by decide, by decide, rfl⟩, ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩,
    ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩⟩

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10: the corpus verdict is `reject` (O4.7: "`g` détenue par `f0`, son
anchor effectif `root_T` passe en `f1`"). Effective verdict of the model: `ok`. In `f1`,
`transfer(M, M′)` by context 0 is an `ok` step of Spec 1 §63 re-indexed; after it, the effective
anchor of `g` (authority 4) is in frame 1, which is not an ancestor of frame 0 holding `g`
(`EffAnchorOKC` fails for `g` and its holder frame), and `exitFrameC(f1)` is rejected. The
positive twin (`M′` local of `f0`) is `Ern.Concurrency.EncapTraces.traceB`. -/
theorem S10_1_ok : opStepC KM (.transfer 0 7) 0 r3 (.ok r4) ∧
    Encap L0 (r3, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) (.kernel 0 (.transfer 0 7)) ∧
    ¬ EffAnchorOKC r4 4 (some 0) ∧ opStepC KM .exit 0 r4 .reject :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, (by decide : TransferExcl L0 (r3, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) 0), by decide,
    ⟨by decide, .reject (by decide)⟩⟩

/-- The steps of S10 form an `EncapsulatedTrace` from the initial state (WC4 C22, C23): the
effective verdict of `S10_1_ok` is an `ok` of the machine with the library, not only of the
kernel. -/
theorem s10_trace : EncapsulatedTrace KM L0 (x0, [], [])
    [.kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .modify), .kernel 0 (.store 3 1), .newMutex 0 3, .acquire 0 0,
     .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [1, 2] .modify),
     .kernel 0 (.enter [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]),
     .kernel 0 (.transfer 0 7)] (r4, [⟨3, some 4⟩], []) := by
  have h := mx3_trace.snoc (lbl := .acquire 0 0) (st' := (r1, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) trivial
    (.acquire s10_setup.1)
  have h := h.snoc (lbl := .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [1, 2] .modify))
    (st' := (r2, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) (by decide : ∀ e ∈ ([⟨3, some 4⟩] : SyncReg), e.Live r1 →
      0 ≠ e.guarded) (.kernel s10_setup.2.1)
  have h := h.snoc (lbl := .kernel 0 (.enter [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]))
    (st' := (r3, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) trivial (.kernel s10_setup.2.2)
  exact h.snoc (lbl := .kernel 0 (.transfer 0 7)) (st' := (r4, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) S10_1_ok.2.1
    (.kernel S10_1_ok.1)

end Ern.Concurrency.Corpus
theorem mx_steps : opStepC KM (.derive 1 [3] .modify) 0 x0 (.ok x1) ∧
    opStepC KM (.store 3 1) 0 x1 (.ok x2) ∧ NewMutexOk KM L0 [] x2 [] 0 3 (x2, regX) ∧
    ControlOf L0 x2 ⟨3, none⟩ = some 2 ∧
    opStepC KM (.derive 0 [1, 2] .observe) 0 x2 (.ok x3) ∧ SpawnStep x3 0 [4] [] (.ok x4) :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩, ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩,
    by decide, ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩, ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩⟩

/-- `MX₃` (`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §0) is reached from the initial state by an `EncapsulatedTrace`
(WC4 C22, C23). -/
theorem mx3_trace : EncapsulatedTrace KM L0 (x0, [], [])
    [.kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .modify), .kernel 0 (.store 3 1), .newMutex 0 3] (x2, regX, []) :=
  .cons (fun e he => by cases he) (.kernel mx_steps.1) <|
  .cons trivial (.kernel mx_steps.2.1) <| .cons trivial (.newMutex mx_steps.2.2.1) .nil

/-- `MX₄` (`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §0) is reached from the initial state by an `EncapsulatedTrace`
(WC4 C22, C23). -/
theorem mx4_trace : EncapsulatedTrace KM L0 (x0, [], [])
    [.kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .modify), .kernel 0 (.store 3 1), .newMutex 0 3,
     .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [1, 2] .observe), .spawn 0 [4] []] (x4, regX, []) :=
  .cons (fun e he => by cases he) (.kernel mx_steps.1) <|
  .cons trivial (.kernel mx_steps.2.1) <| .cons trivial (.newMutex mx_steps.2.2.1) <|
  .cons (by decide : ∀ e ∈ regX, e.Live x2 → 0 ≠ e.guarded) (.kernel mx_steps.2.2.2.2.1) <|
  .cons trivial (.spawn mx_steps.2.2.2.2.2) .nil

/-- In `MX₄`, `root_M` has effective mode `Observe` on `slot` and `lock` (Spec 1 §43.4) and
`CtrlRight` holds for frame 0 and for the initial frame 1 of context 1 (`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §0,

## C2. Concurrent State and External Contracts

The candidate concurrent authority machine is:

\[ S_C=(C,F_C,P,I,A,D) \]

where:

- `C` identifies execution contexts and their lifecycle states.
- `F_C` contains their local frame stacks and extended frame-parent relation.
- `P`, `I`, `A`, and `D` retain their meanings from Spec 1.

The authority and dependency state is globally coherent. Library administration states, including synchronization registries, remain separate from `S_C`.

The concurrency specification introduces an external contract extension `K_C` with a projection to the unchanged Spec 1 contract `K`. A synchronization registry may be supplied as an **external argument** to `K_C.SyncAuthorized` by the reference abstraction. It does not become a component of `S_C`. This is the candidate P2 convention, subject to formal verification of its state-dependent soundness.

For an inherited operation executed by context `c`, all occurrences of “the current frame” refer to the top of the live local stack of `c`. References to live frames, usable places, ownership chains, authority holders and orphan conditions range over the globally live frame structure. An inherited `K.Satisfiable` obligation for a context-executed allocation is evaluated on the `S₃` view of the executing context (`SC.view(s,c)` in the exploratory model); this is candidate P1 and must preserve the soundness requirements of Spec 1's unchanged `K`.

For a single context with no active concurrent mechanism, these interpretations and the projection of `K_C` must coincide with Spec 1.

## C19. Synchronized Administration

A grant protecting an administrative value may permit `MetaRight` only when it provides exercisable `Modify` over every required leaf of that administrative value.

The grant must therefore cover the entire required administrative footprint.

This does not bypass Spec 1 §36.

Issuance, recycling, and reset operations retain their existing authority and dependency restrictions.

The lifetime of a block issued during synchronized administration is determined by its actual origin chain, holders, anchors, and ownership relations, not merely by the lifetime of the synchronization grant.

---

# III. Invariants and Correspondence

## C20. Concurrent Frame and Authority Well-Formedness

`ConcurrentWF` extends frame well-formedness to multiple local stacks and one global parent relationship.

It must preserve the applicable structural, ownership, holder, and authority conditions of Spec 1.

Every inherited transition and every new concurrent transition must preserve the applicable global invariants.

Reparenting must preserve extended ancestry and validity properties.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
1:## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena
10:6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).
29:6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

instance (s : SC) (c : Nat) : Decidable (s.Live c) := by unfold SC.Live; infer_instance

/-- Local stack of context `c` if it is live, empty otherwise (WC4 C2, C3). -/
def SC.stk (s : SC) (c : Nat) : List Nat :=
  match s.C[c]? with
  | some x => if x.life = .live then x.stack else []
  | none => []

/-- Parent of the initial frame of context `c` (WC4 C3). -/
def SC.ctxParent (s : SC) (c : Nat) : Option Nat := (s.C[c]?).bind (·.parent)

/-- Globally live frames: the frames of the stacks of live contexts (WC4 C2). -/
def SC.frames (s : SC) : List Nat := (List.range s.C.length).flatMap s.stk

/-- The kernel components of `s` as an `S3` whose stack lists the globally live frames (WC4 C2:
references to live frames consider the globally live frame structure). -/
def SC.flat (s : SC) : S3 :=
  { F := s.frames, nF := s.nF, P := s.P, I := s.I, A := s.A, D := s.D, dead := s.dead,
    pins := s.pins }

/-- The `S3` seen by executing context `c` (WC4 C2): the stack of `c` first, so that the current
frame is the top of its local stack, followed by the other globally live frames. It is the `S₃`
view of WC4 C2 (candidate P1) on which `K.Satisfiable` of an `alloc` executed by `c` is evaluated
(`alloc_ok_satisfiable`, `alloc_fail_unsatisfiable`). -/
def SC.view (s : SC) (c : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s.flat with F := s.stk c ++ s.frames.filter fun f => decide (f ∉ s.stk c) }

/-- Kernel components of an `S3` written back into `s`; contexts unchanged (WC4 C2). -/
def SC.set (s : SC) (t : S3) : SC :=
  { s with nF := t.nF, P := t.P, I := t.I, A := t.A, D := t.D, dead := t.dead, pins := t.pins }

/-!
# Theorems 2, 4 and 7 on labelled steps and traces (WC4 C20–C23; Spec 1 §55, §56)

`Ern.Concurrency.Reparent` and `Ern.Concurrency.SyncInit`:

* theorem 2 for every labelled step of the kernel with the synchronization and arena libraries,
  the by-value composite included (`lstep_kInvCA`);
* theorems 2, 4 and 7 together along an `EncapsulatedTrace` (WC4 C22, C23; Spec 1 §55, §56):
  `KInvCA`, `SyncState`, `AdminSep` and `ArenaInvC` (`trace_inv`, `trace_preserves`,
  `encapsulated_inv`, `encapsulated_arenaInv`).
-/

import Lean
import Ern
open Lean Meta Elab Command
elab "#audit3" : command => do
  let env ← getEnv
  let mut bad := 0
  let mut n := 0
  let mut nPub := 0
  for (nm, ci) in env.constants.toList do
    let s := nm.toString
    unless (s.startsWith "Ern.Concurrency" || s.startsWith "_private.Ern.Concurrency") do continue
    unless ci matches .thmInfo _ do continue
    n := n + 1
    unless nm.isInternal do nPub := nPub + 1
    let axs ← liftCoreM <| collectAxioms nm
    let extra := axs.filter (fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound)
    if extra.size > 0 then
      bad := bad + 1
      IO.println s!"BAD {nm} {extra.toList}"
  IO.println s!"Concurrency theorems: {n} (non-internal {nPub}), outside propext/Quot.sound: {bad}"
  let mods := [`Ern.Concurrency.ArenaPreserve, `Ern.Concurrency.ArenaConservativity, `Ern.Concurrency.RealizeSound,
    `Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.MX, `Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.AR, `Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.Frames,
    `Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.S10, `Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.Witness]
  for mn in mods do
    let mut m := 0
    let mut mp := 0
    for (nm, ci) in env.constants.toList do
      unless ci matches .thmInfo _ do continue
      let some idx := env.getModuleIdxFor? nm | continue
      unless env.header.moduleNames[idx.toNat]! == mn do continue
      m := m + 1
      unless nm.isInternal do mp := mp + 1
    IO.println s!"{mn}: {m} theorems ({mp} non-internal)"
#audit3

example : LRun KM L0 (x0, [], [])
    [.kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .modify), .kernel 0 (.store 3 1), .newMutex 0 3,
     .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [1, 2] .observe), .spawn 0 [4] [], .deriveSync 1 3,
     .kernel 1 (.release 5), .acquire 1 0]
    (deriveSyncEff x5r 1 3, [⟨3, some 6⟩], []) := by
  have h := mx4_trace.run
  have e := W_C22_2_encap.1
  have r := W_C22_2_reenable
  -- append three steps
  have h1 : LRun KM L0 (x4, regX, []) [.deriveSync 1 3, .kernel 1 (.release 5), .acquire 1 0]
      (deriveSyncEff x5r 1 3, [⟨3, some 6⟩], []) :=
    .cons (.deriveSync e) (.cons (.kernel r.1) (.cons (.acquire r.2.2.2) .nil))
  clear e r
  -- concatenate
  have app : ∀ {a b c : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} {l1 l2}, LRun KM L0 a l1 b → LRun KM L0 b l2 c →
      LRun KM L0 a (l1 ++ l2) c := by
    intro a b c l1 l2 h1 h2
    induction h1 with
    | nil => exact h2
    | cons s _ ih => exact .cons s (ih h2)
  exact app h h1

-- derivative 5 is the deriveSync product: origin 3, held by context 1's frame, Modify, active in x5
#eval (x4.A.length, x5.A.length, (x5.A[5]?).map (fun a => (a.origin, a.mode == .modify)))
#eval decide (x5r.flat.Active 5)
#eval decide (x5.flat.Active 5)
-- wst: root authorities and holders
#eval w0.A.map (fun a => (a.holder, a.footprint))
#eval decide (slotOf w2 1 = some 8)
#eval decide (slotOf w0 1 = some 1)
-- S10: start state is the initial one
example : x0 = SC.ofS3 (S3.init mxst) := rfl
EOF

input.message:
**Verdict: changes.** There is one wrong line reference in the report, and the code fixes check out. Nothing blocks.

**Re-run results (all at 33b672f)**
- `lake build`: "Build completed successfully (66 jobs)".
- The AGENTS grep prints nothing (exit 1).
- `Audit3.lean`: "Concurrency theorems: 1092 (non-internal 835), outside propext/Quot.sound: 0". This matches the report's numbers.
- `lake env lean` on `Corpus/{MX,S10,Witness,AR}`, `Reachable` and `SyncLib` gives no output, so no warnings.

**1. `W_C22_2_reenable`: it is a real counter-trace.**
- It starts from the same state as `W_C22_2_encap` (`x5`, `regX` with `grant = none`).
- Authority 5 is what the raw `deriveSync` creates. Scratch `#eval` gives `x4.A.length = 5`, and `A[5]` has origin 3 (`guarded`) and mode Modify. It is active in `x5` and inactive in `x5r`.
- `Encap` admits `.kernel 1 (.release 5)` through the `_ => True` case (`SyncLib.lean` `Encap`).
- `AcquireOk` with a concrete post-state is the same enabledness notion that `S2_4_wait` negates.
- In scratch (`review-2/Check.lean`) I built the whole thing as a single `LRun` from `(x0,[],[])`: the `mx4_trace` steps, then `.deriveSync 1 3`, `.kernel 1 (.release 5)` and `.acquire 1 0`. It typechecks.
- Quotes are correct. The corpus says "`acquire(e)` plus jamais habilitée" (C13.9/C14) and P8 quotes it exactly. The WC4 C15 fragment in the docstring matches ERN_WC4.md:296 ("This grant is ordinary after creation … legal release").
- The fix adds no unreported interpretation: P8 is now a disagreement, consistent with the corpus §4 rule.
- Nit: P8's "Lecture" says "le blocage dure tant que la dérivée est active". That is a general claim with no proof; only this one instance is shown. Also, the A.3 row says "`acquire` redevient habilité" without "par le contexte 1", which P8 does state.

**2. S10: correct.**
- `s10_trace` starts at `(x0,[],[])`, and `x0 = SC.ofS3 (S3.init mxst)` (`rfl`).
- Every step has an `Encap` proof: `mx3_trace`, then `.acquire` (True), `derive 0` (`decide`), `.enter` (True), and `transfer 0 7` (`TransferExcl` by `decide`).
- The last step is the transfer from `r3`, which is exactly the step the corpus expects to be `reject`. The trace ends in `(r4, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])`.
- P2's description is accurate. The line references are right: `S10.lean:43` and `:52`.

**3. W-C22.3 (b): correct.**
- The new `wst` entries 7–11 form `M′ = {slot′ = {a′, b′}, lock′}`, all `Uninit`. Root authorities are `[frame0:[2,3,4]], [place1:[5]], [frame0:[6]], [frame0:[9,10,11]]`, which matches the docstring.
- `W_C22_3b_ok` is `transfer(0,7)`, i.e. `transfer(M, M′)`, from `w0` (`slot = {a,b}`). `TransferExcl` holds and `SlotInit w2` holds (`slotOf w2 1 = some 8`).
- Entries 0–6 are unchanged and M′ is appended at the end, so `W_C22_3b_encap` proves the same thing as before: source 2 (a), destination 6 (Z), `guarded` 1.

**4. Docstrings: accurate.**
- `NewArenaPreC.wf3`: `SC.flat` uses `F := s.frames`, the globally live frames, which matches WC4 C2.
- `Label` now has the arena constructors.
- The new `Reachable` title is correct (the module covers T7 and §55/§56). Pre-existing nit: its unchanged "Assembly of …" line still omits `ArenaPreserve`, which `trace_inv` uses.

**5. Report**
- **Finding (low, report error):** in the A.3 S2 row (`spec2-m3.md:196`), the range is "`S2_1_ok` … `S2_3_ok` (`Corpus/MX:136`–`136`)". `S2_1_ok` is at `MX.lean:128`. The old text, `MX:128`–`136`, was correct, so this fix introduced the error. It also makes "contrôlés par script" in « Ce qui n'est pas vérifié » inaccurate.
- I checked every other changed `name (Module:line)` reference by script and by opening each line. All are correct, including `Label` 497, `LStep` 517, `LRun`/`EncapsulatedTrace` 589/599, `AR:175`, `Witness:48/66/83/109/136/143`, `MX:346/365/408/424/432`, `Reparent:654/671`, `SyncLib:618/626/646/668`, and `SyncInit:1017`.
